traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Washingtonia filifera (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.47 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.47, branches 0.49. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.note: Sargent (1922, Washingtonia filamentosa, i.e. W. filifera, pp. 104-105): leaves 5 to 6 ft long and 4 to 5 ft wide, divided nearly to the middle into recurved segments, on petioles 4 to 6 ft (1.2 to 1.8 m), so a frond about 3.4 m, 0.45 of it petiole; a short rachis (costa 0.12); a trunk to 50 to 60 ft and 2 to 3 ft through (trunk_radius 0.42 m); a broad crown of erect and spreading, finally pendulous leaves (hang 50 degrees over a frond's life, the segments arching down 30 degrees to the fan's edges), with a thick thatch of dead pendant leaves descending in a cone from the crown nearly to the ground (skirt, dead_life 60). Other values set by hand from general knowledge of the species, not fitted to measurements. Sargent (p. 104) gives the petioles' bases as thick, broad, concave, bright chestnut-brown sheaths of a network of fibres, 16 to 18 in long and 12 to 14 in wide (p. 105): each frond clasps the stem 0.45 m below its foot with four cards (sheath_length, shaft_cards), so the crown's leaf bases hide the stem's top where it stood bare.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 8 m at 30 years and 17 m at 60. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: grey-green fans, a straw-brown skirt, a grey trunk. Shades as linear light (2026-10-16), from Sargent (1922, p. 104-105): leaves light green [0.1, 0.19, 0.06], sheaths bright chestnut-brown, the trunk's rind light red-brown, the thatch straw-brown; the by-eye values had been written as screen (sRGB) shades and drew near white. Each segment's card droops 35 degrees along its free part (2026-10-18), after the family's rule has turned the free part down where it parts from the palman, where the whole card had drooped 55 from the fan's centre; its dead fans are drawn as the genus draws them, hanging closed against the trunk.
